sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmaho viṣṇuṃ bhagavantaṃ sanātanam saṃpūjya varadaṃ devaṃ mahādevam athābravīt
english: Then the Grandsire, having worshipped the boon-granting Lord Viṣṇu, the eternal, and the great god Mahādeva, spoke thus.

sanskrit: atra sādhv anukampāṃ vai kartum arhasi kevalam saṃkaro na bhaved atra yathā vai tad vidhīyatām
english: Here you ought, of your sole grace, to show compassion: so ordain it that this confusion of all order may not come to pass.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān dhyātvā ciraṃ śūlajaṭādharaḥ ātmānam ātmanā daṇḍam asṛjad devasattamaḥ
english: Then that Lord, bearer of the trident and the matted locks, having meditated long, the best of gods, brought forth from himself, by himself, the Rod of Chastisement.

sanskrit: tasmāc ca dharmacaraṇāṃ nītiṃ devīṃ sarasvatīm asṛjad daṇḍanītiḥ sā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
english: And from that he brought forth Policy, the goddess Sarasvatī, who treads the way of dharma; that science of governance by the Rod is renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ sa bhagavān dhyātvā ciraṃ śūlavarāyudhaḥ tasya tasya nikāyasya cakāraikaikam īśaram
english: Again that Lord, whose chief weapon is the trident, having meditated long, appointed for each several order of beings its own particular ruler.

sanskrit: devānām īśvaraṃ cakre devaṃ daśaśatekṣaṇam yamaṃ vaivasvataṃ cāpi pitṝṇām akarot patim
english: He made the thousand-eyed god the lord of the deities, and Yama, son of Vivasvat, he made the lord of the ancestral fathers.

sanskrit: dhanānāṃ rakṣasāṃ cāpi kuberam api ceśvaram parvatānāṃ patiṃ meruṃ saritāṃ ca mahodadhim
english: Kubera he made lord of riches and of the rākṣasas; Meru he made lord of the mountains, and the great ocean lord of the rivers.

sanskrit: apāṃ rājye surāṇāṃ ca vidadhe varuṇaṃ prabhum mṛtyuṃ prāṇeśvaram atho tejasāṃ ca hutāśanam
english: Over the realm of the waters and of the gods he set Varuṇa as sovereign; Death he made lord of living breaths, and the Oblation-eater (Agni) lord of the fiery energies.

sanskrit: rudrāṇām api ceśānaṃ goptāraṃ vidadhe prabhuḥ mahātmānaṃ mahādevaṃ viśālākṣaṃ sanātanam
english: As lord and guardian of the Rudras the Lord appointed the great-souled Mahādeva, the wide-eyed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭham īśaṃ viprāṇāṃ vasūnāṃ jātavedasam tejasāṃ bhāskaraṃ cakre nakṣatrāṇāṃ niśākaram
english: Vasiṣṭha he made lord of the brāhmaṇas, Jātavedas (Agni) of the Vasus; the Sun he made lord of the radiances, and the Moon of the constellations.

sanskrit: vīrudhām aṃśumantaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ ca prabhuṃ varam kumāraṃ dvādaśabhujaṃ skandaṃ rājānam ādiśat
english: The rayed one (Soma) he made lord of the herbs; and the youthful, twelve-armed Skanda he ordained as the chief lord and king of the spirit-hosts.

sanskrit: kālaṃ sarveśam akarot saṃhāravinayātmakam mṛtyoś caturvibhāgasya duḥkhasya ca sukhasya ca
english: He made Time the lord of all, whose nature is destruction and restraint, master of fourfold Death, of sorrow, and of joy.

sanskrit: īśvaraḥ sarvadehas tu rājarājo dhanādhipaḥ sarveṣām eva rudrāṇāṃ śūlapāṇir iti śrutiḥ
english: The Lord whose body is all things, the king of kings, the master of wealth, the trident-bearer, is the ruler of all the Rudras: so runs the sacred tradition.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ brahmaṇaḥ putram anujātaṃ kṣupaṃ dadau prajānām adhipaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadharmabhṛtām api
english: To that one Kṣupa, the son born after Brahmā, he gave dominion, making him the foremost overlord of creatures and of all who uphold dharma.

sanskrit: mahādevas tatas tasmin vṛtte yajñe yathāvidhi daṇḍaṃ dharmasya goptāraṃ viṣṇave satkṛtaṃ dadau
english: Then Mahādeva, when that sacrifice was concluded according to rule, gave the Rod, the guardian of dharma, with due honour, to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: viṣṇur aṅgirase prādād aṅgirā munisattamaḥ prādād indramarīcibhyāṃ marīcir bhṛgave dadau
english: Viṣṇu gave it to Aṅgiras; Aṅgiras, best of sages, gave it to Indra and Marīci; and Marīci gave it to Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: bhṛgur dadāv ṛṣibhyas tu taṃ daṇḍaṃ dharmasaṃhitam ṛṣayo lokapālebhyo lokapālāḥ kṣupāya ca
english: Bhṛgu gave that Rod, conjoined with dharma, to the seers; the seers gave it to the guardians of the worlds, and the world-guardians to Kṣupa.

sanskrit: kṣupas tu manave prādād ādityatanayāya ca putrebhyaḥ śrāddhadevas tu sūkṣmadharmārthakāraṇāt taṃ dadau sūryaputras tu manur vai rakṣaṇātmakam
english: Kṣupa gave it to Manu, the son of the Sun; and the Lord of the Śrāddha (Manu), to fulfil the subtle ends of dharma, gave it to his sons — that Manu, the Sun's son, bestowed it as the very principle of protection.

sanskrit: vibhajya daṇḍaḥ kartavyo dharmeṇa na yadṛcchayā durvācā nigraho bandho hiraṇyaṃ bāhyataḥkriyā
english: Chastisement must be apportioned and meted out by dharma, not at whim: harsh rebuke, restraint, imprisonment, fines of gold, and outward correction —

sanskrit: vyaṅgatvaṃ ca śarīrasya vadho vā nālpakāraṇāt śarīrapīḍās tās tās tu dehatyāgo vivāsanam
english: and maiming of the body, or death — but not for a trifling cause — these several bodily torments, the surrender of life, and banishment.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyā ca daṇḍo 'sau prajā jāgarti pālayan indro jāgarti bhagavān indrād agnir vibhāvasuḥ
english: In due succession that Rod keeps watch, guarding the people: Lord Indra keeps watch, and from Indra, Agni the radiant.

sanskrit: agner jāgarti varuṇo varuṇāc ca prajāpatiḥ prajāpates tato dharmo jāgarti vinayātmakaḥ
english: After Agni, Varuṇa keeps watch, and after Varuṇa, Prajāpati; and after Prajāpati, Dharma keeps watch, whose essence is discipline.

sanskrit: dharmāc ca brahmaṇaḥ putro vyavasāyaḥ sanātanaḥ vyavasāyāt tatas tejo jāgarti paripālayan
english: After Dharma keeps watch Resolve, the eternal son of Brahmā; and after Resolve, fiery energy keeps watch, protecting all.

sanskrit: oṣadhyas tejasas tasmād oṣadhibhyaś ca parvatāḥ parvatebhyaś ca jāgarti raso rasaguṇāt tathā
english: After that energy the herbs keep watch, and after the herbs the mountains; and after the mountains, Sap keeps watch, by virtue of the quality of savour.

sanskrit: jāgarti nirṛtir devī jyotīṃṣi nirṛter api vedāḥ pratiṣṭhā jyotirbhyas tato hayaśirāḥ prabhuḥ
english: The goddess Nirṛti keeps watch, and after Nirṛti the heavenly lights; the Vedas are the foundation after the lights, and then the Horse-headed Lord (Hayaśiras).

sanskrit: brahmā pitāmahas tasmāj jāgarti prabhur avyayaḥ pitāmahān mahādevo jāgarti bhagavāñ śivaḥ
english: After him Brahmā the Grandsire keeps watch, the imperishable Lord; and after the Grandsire, the great god, Lord Śiva, keeps watch.

sanskrit: viśvedevāḥ śivāc cāpi viśvebhyaś ca tatharṣayaḥ ṛṣibhyo bhagavān somaḥ somād devāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: After Śiva, the All-Gods, and after the All-Gods, the seers; after the seers, Lord Soma, and after Soma, the eternal deities.

sanskrit: devebhyo brāhmaṇā loke jāgratīty upadhāraya brāhmaṇebhyaś ca rājanyā lokān rakṣanti dharmataḥ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva kṣatriyebhyaḥ sanātanam
english: After the deities, the brāhmaṇas keep watch in the world — know this well — and after the brāhmaṇas, the kṣatriyas guard the worlds by dharma; the unmoving and the moving alike eternally rest upon the kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: prajā jāgrati loke 'smin daṇḍo jāgarti tāsu ca sarvasaṃkṣepako daṇḍaḥ pitāmahasamaḥ prabhuḥ
english: The people keep watch in this world, and over them keeps watch the Rod; that Rod, which gathers all things into itself, is a lord equal to the Grandsire.

sanskrit: jāgarti kālaḥ pūrvaṃ ca madhye cānte ca bhārata īśvaraḥ sarvalokasya mahādevaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: Time keeps watch at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, O Bhārata — the Lord of all the worlds, the great god, Prajāpati.

sanskrit: devadevaḥ śivaḥ śarvo jāgarti satataṃ prabhuḥ kapardī śaṃkaro rudro bhavaḥ sthāṇur umāpatiḥ
english: The God of gods, Śiva, Śarva, keeps watch forever, the Lord — the matted-haired one, Śaṃkara, Rudra, Bhava, Sthāṇu, the consort of Umā.

sanskrit: ity eṣa daṇḍo vikhyāta ādau madhye tathāvare bhūmipālo yathānyāyaṃ vartetānena dharmavit
english: Thus is this Rod proclaimed, at the beginning, the middle, and the last; by it let the guardian of the earth, the knower of dharma, conduct himself according to justice.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca itīdaṃ vasuhomasya śṛṇuyād yo mataṃ naraḥ śrutvā ca samyag varteta sa kāmān āpnuyān nṛpaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Whatever man should hear this teaching of Vasuhoma, and having heard it should conduct himself rightly — that king shall attain all his desires.

sanskrit: iti te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yo daṇḍo manujarṣabha niyantā sarvalokasya dharmākrāntasya bhārata
english: Thus have I declared to you, O bull among men, all concerning that Rod, the restrainer of every world that has gone astray from dharma, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tāta dharmārthakāmānāṃ śrotum icchāmi niścayam lokayātrā hi kārtsnyena triṣv eteṣu pratiṣṭhitā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Father, I wish to hear the settled truth concerning dharma, wealth, and desire; for the whole conduct of life in this world rests entirely upon these three.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmāḥ kiṃmūlās trayāṇāṃ prabhavaś ca kaḥ anyonyaṃ cānuṣajjante vartante ca pṛthak pṛthak
english: In what are dharma, wealth, and desire rooted, and what is the source of these three? How do they cleave to one another, and yet operate each apart?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yadā te syuḥ sumanaso lokasaṃsthārthaniścaye kālaprabhavasaṃsthāsu sajjante ca trayas tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: When men are well-minded toward the discernment of the world's right ordering, then the three cleave together in their arisings, abidings, and ceasings within Time.

sanskrit: dharmamūlas tu deho 'rthaḥ kāmo 'rthaphalam ucyate saṃkalpamūlās te sarve saṃkalpo viṣayātmakaḥ
english: The body is rooted in dharma; wealth is its means, and desire is called the fruit of wealth. All these are rooted in resolve, and resolve has the sense-objects for its essence.

sanskrit: viṣayāś caiva kārtsnyena sarva āhārasiddhaye mūlam etat trivargasya nivṛttir mokṣa ucyate
english: And the sense-objects, one and all, serve wholly for the sustaining of life; this is the root of the triad — while their cessation is called liberation (mokṣa).

sanskrit: dharmaḥ śarīrasaṃguptir dharmārthaṃ cārtha iṣyate kāmo ratiphalaś cātra sarve caite rajasvalāḥ
english: Dharma is the safeguarding of the body; wealth is sought for the sake of dharma; and desire here has delight for its fruit — yet all these are charged with the quality of passion (rajas).

sanskrit: saṃnikṛṣṭāṃś cared enān na cainān manasā tyajet vimuktas tamasā sarvān dharmādīn kāmanaiṣṭhikān
english: He should pursue these as they lie near to hand, yet not abandon them in his mind; freed from darkness (tamas), he should hold to them all — dharma and the rest — making desire their goal.

sanskrit: śreṣṭhabuddhis trivargasya yad ayaṃ prāpnuyāt kṣaṇāt buddhyā budhyed ihārthe na tad ahnā tu nikṛṣṭayā
english: He of best understanding, regarding the triad, should grasp at once by the higher intellect what is to be known in any matter, and not by the meaner intellect, plodding day by day.

sanskrit: apadhyānamalo dharmo malo 'rthasya nigūhanam saṃpramodamalaḥ kāmo bhūyaḥ svaguṇavartitaḥ
english: The taint of dharma is evil intent; the taint of wealth is hoarding; the taint of desire is reckless revelry — each, moreover, turning back upon its own quality.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam kāmandasya ca saṃvādam aṅgāriṣṭhasya cobhayoḥ
english: On this point too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue of both Kāmanda and Aṅgāriṣṭha.

sanskrit: kāmandam ṛṣim āsīnam abhivādya narādhipaḥ aṅgāriṣṭho 'tha papraccha kṛtvā samayaparyayam
english: Having saluted the seer Kāmanda as he sat, and observing the proper occasion, the king Aṅgāriṣṭha then put his question.

sanskrit: yaḥ pāpaṃ kurute rājā kāmamohabalātkṛtaḥ pratyāsannasya tasyarṣe kiṃ syāt pāpapraṇāśanam
english: When a king commits a sin, driven by the force of desire and delusion, O seer, what may serve to destroy the sin of such a man when he comes to repent?

sanskrit: adharmo dharma iti ha yo 'jñānād ācared iha taṃ cāpi prathitaṃ loke kathaṃ rājā nivartayet
english: And when, out of ignorance, a king practises unrighteousness here thinking it righteousness, and it has become notorious in the world, how should he turn back from it?

sanskrit: kāmanda uvāca yo dharmārthau samutsṛjya kāmam evānuvartate sa dharmārthaparityāgāt prajñānāśam ihārchati
english: Kāmanda said: He who, casting off dharma and wealth, pursues desire alone, comes by that abandonment of dharma and wealth to the ruin of his wisdom in this world.

sanskrit: prajñāpraṇāśako mohas tathā dharmārthanāśakaḥ tasmān nāstikatā caiva durācāraś ca jāyate
english: Delusion is the destroyer of wisdom, and likewise the destroyer of dharma and wealth; from it, in turn, are born unbelief and wicked conduct.

sanskrit: durācārān yadā rājā praduṣṭān na niyacchati tasmād udvijate lokaḥ sarpād veśmagatād iva
english: When a king does not restrain the depraved men of evil conduct, the people shrink from him as from a serpent that has entered the house.

sanskrit: taṃ prajā nānuvartante brāhmaṇā na ca sādhavaḥ tataḥ saṃkṣayam āpnoti tathā vadhyatvam eti ca
english: The people no longer follow him, nor the brāhmaṇas, nor the virtuous; thereupon he meets with utter ruin, and comes besides to be slain.

sanskrit: apadhvastas tv avamato duḥkhaṃ jīvati jīvitam jīvec ca yad apadhvastas tac chuddhaṃ maraṇaṃ bhavet
english: Cast down and despised, he lives a life of misery; and the very life that such a fallen man lives is but death made plain.

sanskrit: atraitad āhur ācāryāḥ pāpasya ca nibarhaṇam sevitavyā trayī vidyā satkāro brāhmaṇeṣu ca
english: On this matter the teachers declare the means of expiating sin: the threefold sacred knowledge (the Vedas) is to be cultivated, and honour shown to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: mahāmanā bhaved dharme vivahec ca mahākule brāhmaṇāṃś cāpi seveta kṣamāyuktān manasvinaḥ
english: He should be high-minded in dharma, and marry into a noble house; he should also wait upon brāhmaṇas endowed with forbearance and wisdom.

sanskrit: japed udakaśīlaḥ syāt sumukho nānyad āsthitaḥ dharmānvitān saṃpraviśed bahiḥ kṛtvaiva duṣkṛtīn
english: He should murmur prayers, be given to ablutions, gracious of countenance, set upon naught else; he should consort with the righteous, having shut the evildoers out.

sanskrit: prasādayen madhuraya vācāpy atha ca karmaṇā ity asmīti vaden nityaṃ pareṣāṃ kīrtayan guṇān
english: He should conciliate others with sweet speech and likewise with deeds, saying ever 'Thus am I,' while proclaiming the virtues of others.

sanskrit: apāpo hy evam ācāraḥ kṣipraṃ bahumato bhavet pāpāny api ca kṛcchrāṇi śamayen nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For one of such sinless conduct soon becomes held in high esteem, and quells even grievous sins — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: guravo 'pi paraṃ dharmaṃ yad brūyus tat tathā kuru gurūṇāṃ hi prasādād dhi śreyaḥ param avāpsyasi
english: Whatever supreme dharma the elders may declare, that do accordingly; for through the grace of the elders you shall attain the highest good.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ime janā naraśreṣṭha praśaṃsanti sadā bhuvi dharmasya śīlam evādau tato me saṃśayo mahān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: These men, O best of men, ever praise upon the earth, before all else, good character as the foundation of dharma; thence arises in me a great doubt.

sanskrit: yadi tac chakyam asmābhir jñātuṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara śrotum icchāmi tat sarvaṃ yathaitad upalabhyate
english: If it can be understood by us, O foremost of the upholders of dharma, I wish to hear all of it — how this good character is to be acquired.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu prāpyate śīlaṃ śrotum icchāmi bhārata kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ ca tat proktaṃ brūhi me vadatāṃ vara
english: How then is good character attained? I wish to hear, O Bhārata; and by what marks is it described? Tell me, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca purā duryodhaneneha dhṛtarāṣṭrāya mānada ākhyātaṃ tapyamānena śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatām
english: Bhīṣma said: Long ago, O bestower of honour, Duryodhana here told this to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, tormented as he was at the sight of such prosperity come to others.

sanskrit: indraprasthe mahārāja tava sabhrātṛkasya ha sabhāyāṃ cāvahasanaṃ tat sarvaṃ śṛṇu bhārata
english: At Indraprastha, O great king, in the hall of you and your brothers, there was that mockery he suffered — hear all of it, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhavatas tāṃ sabhāṃ dṛṣṭvā samṛddhiṃ cāpy anuttamām duryodhanas tadāsīnaḥ sarvaṃ pitre nyavedayat
english: Having seen that hall of yours and its unsurpassed splendour, Duryodhana, seated then, reported it all to his father.

sanskrit: śrutvā ca dhṛtarāṣṭro 'pi duryodhanavacas tadā abravīt karṇasahitaṃ duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: And Dhṛtarāṣṭra too, having heard Duryodhana's words then, spoke this speech to Duryodhana, who was attended by Karṇa.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ tapyase putra śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ śrutvā tvām anuneṣyāmi yadi samyag bhaviṣyasi
english: Why do you torment yourself, my son? I wish to hear the truth of it; and having heard, I shall console you, if you will but conduct yourself rightly.

sanskrit: yathā tvaṃ mahad aiśvaryaṃ prāptaḥ parapuraṃjaya kiṃkarā bhrātaraḥ sarve mitrāḥ saṃbandhinas tathā
english: You have attained great lordship, O conqueror of hostile cities; all your brothers are at your service, and so are your friends and kinsmen.

sanskrit: ācchādayasi prāvārān aśnāsi piśitodanam ājāneyā vahanti tvāṃ kasmāc chocasi putraka
english: You clothe yourself in fine mantles, you eat rice with meat, thoroughbred steeds bear you along — why then do you grieve, my little son?

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca daśa tāni sahasrāṇi snātakānāṃ mahātmanām bhuñjate rukmapātrīṣu yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: Duryodhana said: Ten thousand high-souled graduate sages dine from vessels of gold in Yudhiṣṭhira's dwelling.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ sabhāṃ divyāṃ divyapuṣpaphalānvitām aśvāṃs tittirakalmāṣān ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: And having seen that celestial hall, furnished with celestial flowers and fruits, the horses dappled like the partridge, and jewels of every kind —

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tāṃ pāṇḍaveyānām ṛddhim indropamāṃ śubhām amitrāṇāṃ sumahatīm anuśocāmi mānada
english: having seen that splendid prosperity of the sons of Pāṇḍu, rivalling Indra's, the vast prosperity of my foes, I grieve, O bestower of honour.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yadīcchasi śriyaṃ tāta yādṛśīṃ tāṃ yudhiṣṭhire viśiṣṭāṃ vā naravyāghra śīlavān bhava putraka
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: If you desire prosperity such as that which is in Yudhiṣṭhira, my son, or even greater, O tiger among men, then be a man of good character, my little son.

sanskrit: śīlena hi trayo lokāḥ śakyā jetuṃ na saṃśayaḥ na hi kiṃ cid asādhyaṃ vai loke śīlavatāṃ bhavet
english: For by good character the three worlds can be conquered — of this there is no doubt; nothing in the world is unattainable for those of good character.

sanskrit: ekarātreṇa māndhātā tryaheṇa janamejayaḥ saptarātreṇa nābhāgaḥ pṛthivīṃ pratipedivān
english: In a single night Māndhātā, in three days Janamejaya, in seven nights Nābhāga, won possession of the whole earth.

sanskrit: ete hi pārthivāḥ sarve śīlavanto damānvitāḥ atas teṣāṃ guṇakrītā vasudhā svayam āgamat
english: For all these kings were men of good character, endowed with self-restraint; therefore the earth, won over by their virtues, came to them of her own accord.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradena purā proktaṃ śīlam āśritya bhārata
english: On this point too they recount this ancient tale, told of old by Nārada concerning good character, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prahrādena hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ mahendrasya mahātmanaḥ śīlam āśritya daityena trailokyaṃ ca vaśīkṛtam
english: By Prahlāda the kingdom of the great-souled Mahendra was wrested away; relying upon good character, that daitya brought the three worlds under his sway.

sanskrit: tato bṛhaspatiṃ śakraḥ prāñjaliḥ samupasthitaḥ uvāca ca mahāprājñaḥ śreya icchāmi veditum
english: Then Śakra, with joined palms, presented himself before Bṛhaspati and, that man of great wisdom, said: 'I wish to know what is the highest good.'

sanskrit: tato bṛhaspatis tasmai jñānaṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ param kathayām āsa bhagavān devendrāya kurūdvaha
english: Then the Lord Bṛhaspati related to him the supreme knowledge that leads to the highest weal, to the lord of the gods, O scion of Kuru.

sanskrit: etāvac chreya ity eva bṛhaspatir abhāṣata indras tu bhūyaḥ papraccha kva viśeṣo bhaved iti
english: 'Thus much is the highest good' — so Bṛhaspati declared; but Indra asked again, 'Wherein might there be something yet greater?'
